items.headline: U.S. Stocks End Mixed on Friday, Major Indices See Weekly Losses as AI Jitters and Geopolitical Concerns Weigh
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed nearly flat and the Dow Jones Industrial Average posted modest gains on Friday, while the Nasdaq Composite declined. All three major indices finished the week lower, influenced by anxieties over AI spending, volatile oil prices due to Middle East hostilities, and new U.S. tariffs.

items.headline: Noodles & Company Soars on Earnings Beat
items.summary: Shares of Noodles & Company surged after the company reported a second-quarter operating profit of $0.18, significantly beating analysts' expectations of a $0.05 loss.

items.headline: Digital Realty Trust Leads Real Estate Sector Gains
items.summary: Digital Realty Trust was a top performer in the S&P 500, benefiting from strong second-quarter revenue growth of 29% to $1.92 billion, surpassing expectations.

items.headline: SLB Climbs on Strong Q2 Profit
items.summary: Oilfield services firm SLB saw its shares rise after reporting second-quarter profits that exceeded analyst expectations.

items.headline: Intel Falls Despite Beating Q2 Estimates
items.summary: Intel shares declined as investors expressed concern over the company's capital expenditure plans related to AI, despite second-quarter results exceeding Wall Street's expectations.

items.headline: American Express Slips on Unchanged Profit Outlook
items.summary: American Express shares fell over 4% as the company's unchanged profit outlook overshadowed a raised 2026 revenue forecast.

items.headline: Alphabet Shares Dip on AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: Alphabet (Google) shares experienced a decline following concerns about significant capital expenditures for AI infrastructure, despite robust revenue growth in its Cloud division.

items.headline: Real Estate and Materials Lead, Tech Lags Amid AI Spending Jitters
items.summary: On Friday, the Real Estate sector led gains, rising 2.36%, bolstered by strong earnings reports and an uptick in new home sales. Materials also performed well, up 1.44%. Conversely, the Information Technology sector was the weakest, falling 0.88%, largely due to a sell-off in semiconductor stocks driven by investor caution over substantial AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Inflation Concerns Resurface Ahead of Fed Meeting; Business Activity Expands
items.summary: Global inflation fears have reignited due to surging energy prices, new U.S. tariffs, and growing AI investment. The Federal Reserve is anticipated to maintain its interest rate target range of 3.50% to 3.75% at its upcoming meeting, with market participants closely monitoring for signals regarding potential rate hikes in September. U.S. business activity saw its fastest expansion in eight months in July, partly attributed to the FIFA World Cup.

items.headline: New US Tariffs Imposed; Oil Prices Volatile Amid Middle East Tensions
items.summary: The U.S. implemented new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports from numerous trading partners, replacing earlier temporary levies. Brent crude oil prices showed significant volatility, falling nearly 4% to $96.78 a barrel on Friday after earlier hitting $102 during the week, influenced by ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

items.headline: Q2 Earnings Season Kicks Off with Mixed Results; Big Tech Reports Loom
items.summary: The second-quarter earnings season commenced with varied outcomes. Tesla ($TSLA) declined 18% over the week after missing Q2 operating profit forecasts, while Intel ($INTC) shares fell nearly 8% on Friday due to AI spending concerns despite beating revenue estimates. Next week will feature critical earnings reports from major tech companies, including Apple, Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Amazon, as well as key AI supply chain players.
